title: Split finite ordered Cech rows for injective etale module sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative ring, and $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], in a universe in which module sheaves form an abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_X$. Let $r\geq0$ and let $U_1,\ldots,U_r$ be an open cover of $X$ (the empty cover is allowed only if $X=\varnothing$). For each nonempty $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $U_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$ and let $u_I:U_I\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion. For an injective $A_X$-module sheaf $J$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], form the finite cochain complex
$$C^p(J)=\bigoplus_{|I|=p+1}u_{I,*}(J|_{U_I})\quad(0\leq p<r),$$
with all other terms zero. Here restriction and direct image are those of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $I=\{i_0<\cdots<i_{p+1}\}$ define
$$(d^ps)_I=\sum_{a=0}^{p+1}(-1)^a s_{I\setminus\{i_a\}}|_{U_I},$$
and augment by the restrictions $J\to C^0(J)$. Then every $C^p(J)$ is injective, and the augmented sequence
$$0\longrightarrow J\longrightarrow C^0(J)\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow C^{r-1}(J)\longrightarrow0$$
is split exact as a sequence of etale $A_X$-module sheaves: it is exact and each short exact sequence between its cycles and its terms has a retraction of the cycle inclusion. For $r=0$ this means $J=0$. No affineness, separatedness, finite-type hypothesis, or finiteness of $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated finite ordered module-sheaf Cech corollary of the exact restriction/extension-by-zero adjunction used in Tag 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open), with Homological Algebra Tags 0136 (lemma-characterize-injectives) and 0137 (lemma-product-injectives) and Cohomology Tag 02FU (lemma-covering-resolution, the Cech sheaf resolution of an open covering of a ringed space, whose proof contracts the augmented complex by inserting a fixed index containing the point); the local insertion argument is paragraph 2 of the current blueprint proof of thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility.

proof.text: For each open $U\subseteq X$ with inclusion $u:U\hookrightarrow X$, $u$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] identifies $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U$, covering families included. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (clause 1), the inverse image $u^{-1}G$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is naturally isomorphic to the restriction $G|_U(V\to U)=G(V\to X)$, which under this equivalence is the localized restriction $j_U^*G$. The coefficients match: applying [lem-pur-ring-presheaf-sheafification-localization] to the constant ring presheaf with value $A$ (the etale site being essentially small in the universe of the statement) gives a unit-compatible ring isomorphism $A_U\cong A_X|_U$. Hence the equivalence keeps section groups, ring sections, actions and restrictions, and $u^{-1}$ on $A_X$-modules is $j_U^*$ on $A_X|_U$-modules; module morphisms are unchanged. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], restriction $u^*=j_U^*$ and its left adjoint $u_!$ are exact. By [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] applied to $u_!\dashv u^*$, $J|_U$ is injective. The adjunction $u^*\dashv u_*$ on the same constant-coefficient module categories is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Apply the same injective-preservation theorem to the exact $u^*$: $u_*(J|_U)$ is injective on $X$. This includes the empty open; sheaves of modules on the empty scheme are zero because their value on its sole object is zero by the empty-cover sheaf axiom.

proof.text: There are finitely many subsets of each cardinality. In an abelian category their direct sum is their product, so [lem-weil-pbc-product-injectives] and step 1 make every displayed $C^p(J)$ injective. The zero terms are injective directly: every map into zero extends by the zero map. Products here are computed sectionwise: a compatible family of tuples glues uniquely by gluing each coordinate, and coordinatewise module operations and projections give the product universal property. For a finite family, summing the coordinate inclusions gives the coproduct universal property too. By the definition of module morphisms in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], these maps are module-linear. Hence on an etale $W\to X$ the term is $\prod_{|I|=p+1}J(W\times_X U_I)$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and the identification $J|_{U_I}(V)=J(V\to X)$ of step 1. All restriction maps used in the differential are module-linear and commute with further restriction. Thus the displayed formulas define morphisms of sheaves. In $d^{p+1}d^p$, each pair of deleted indices $a<b$ occurs with signs $(-1)^{a+b-1}$ and $(-1)^{a+b}$, and identical restriction maps, so cancels. The augmentation followed by $d^0$ is zero by the same restriction identity.

source.place: Tag 02FU (lemma-covering-resolution), construction of the sheaf complex; Homology Tag 0137 (lemma-product-injectives)

proof.text:
Write $C^{-1}=J$ and $d^{-1}$ for the augmentation. Fix $k$ and an etale $W\to X$ factoring through $U_k$. For $p\geq0$ and $c\in C^p(W)$ define $h^pc\in C^{p-1}(W)$ by
$$(h^pc)_T=\begin{cases}0&k\in T,\\(-1)^{b(T)}c_{T\cup\{k\}}&k\notin T,\end{cases}\qquad b(T)=|\{t\in T:t<k\}|,$$
where $|T|=p$; for $p=0$ this is $h^0c=c_{\{k\}}\in J(W)$. The domains agree since $W\times_XU_T=W\times_XU_{T\cup\{k\}}$. Put the out-of-range $h$ equal to zero. On a component indexed by $S$ with $k\in S$, $h^{p+1}d^pc$ is zero and the only nonzero term in $d^{p-1}h^pc$ deletes $k$; its sign is $(-1)^{2b(S\setminus\{k\})}=1$. If $k\notin S$, the term deleting $k$ in $h^{p+1}d^pc$ is $c_S$. For every other deleted index $s\in S$, its position shifts by one exactly when it lies after $k$, whereas $b(S\setminus\{s\})$ drops by one exactly when $s<k$. Consequently its signs in $dh$ and $hd$ are opposite and the restrictions coincide. Thus $dh+hd=1$ in every nonnegative degree, including the top degree; also $h^0d^{-1}=1$ on $J(W)$. These formulas commute with restrictions of $W$.

source.place: Tag 02FU (lemma-covering-resolution), proof by insertion of a fixed covering index; explicit signed version for strictly increasing subsets

proof.text: For any etale $W\to X$, the opens $W_k=W\times_XU_k$ cover $W$. If a section $c\in C^p(W)$ satisfies $d^pc=0$, step 3 gives $c|_{W_k}=d^{p-1}(h^p(c|_{W_k}))$, also for $p=0$ with the augmentation as $d^{-1}$. Thus every kernel section is locally an image section. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so these local lifts say precisely that the homology sheaves vanish. At $J$, a section whose augmentation is zero restricts to zero on every $W_k$, so is zero by the sheaf axiom. This proves exactness at every term and surjectivity onto the final term. When $r=0$, $X$ is empty by hypothesis and $J=0$ by the empty-cover sheaf axiom as in step 1; all conclusions follow. Assume henceforth $r>0$.

source.place: Tag 02FU (lemma-covering-resolution), checking exactness locally; empty-cover endpoint

proof.text: Put $Z^0=J$, identified with $\ker d^0$ by the augmentation, and for $1\leq p<r$ put $Z^p=\ker d^p$, with $d^{r-1}=0$; put $Z^r=0$. Exactness gives $0\to Z^p\xrightarrow{i_p}C^p\xrightarrow{q_p}Z^{p+1}\to0$ for $0\leq p<r$. Inductively $Z^p$ is injective, starting from $J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ses-injective-kernel-splits] to obtain a retraction $\pi_p$ and section $s_p$ with $q_ps_p=1$. The quotient $Z^{p+1}$ is injective because it is a retract of the injective $C^p$ from step 2: for a monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow N$ and $a:M\to Z^{p+1}$, extend $s_pa:M\to C^p$ across $N$ using injectivity and compose the extension with $q_p$. This proves the induction and supplies every required cycle retraction. The left endpoint is an isomorphism onto its image and the right endpoint has zero quotient, so the same reasoning includes both endpoints and $r=1$.

lean.statement: theorem dg_etale_injective_finite_cech_rows (X : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (U : Fin r → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) (J : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) [Injective J] : ∃ (T : ℕ → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (π : ∀ (p : ℕ) (t : Fin (p + 1) ↪o Fin r), T p ⟶ finiteCechOpenTerm A J (alternatingCechIntersection U t)) (d : ∀ p : ℕ, T p ⟶ T (p + 1)) (hdd : ∀ p : ℕ, d p ≫ d (p + 1) = 0) (ε : J ⟶ T 0), (∀ p : ℕ, Nonempty (IsLimit (Fan.mk (T p) (π p)))) ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ) (t : Fin (p + 2) ↪o Fin r) (W : X.Etale) (s : (T p).obj.obj (op W)), ((π (p + 1) t).hom.app (op W)) (((d p).hom.app (op W)) s) = ∑ a : Fin (p + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ a.val • J.obj.map (finiteCechTestInclusion W (alternatingCechIntersection_face_le U p t a)).op (((π p ((Fin.succAboveOrderEmb a).trans t)).hom.app (op W)) s)) ∧ (∀ (t : Fin 1 ↪o Fin r) (W : X.Etale) (s : J.obj.obj (op W)), ((π 0 t).hom.app (op W)) ((ε.hom.app (op W)) s) = J.obj.map (finiteCechTestProjection W (alternatingCechIntersection U t)).op s) ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, r ≤ p → IsZero (T p)) ∧ (∃ hε : ε ≫ d 0 = 0, (ShortComplex.mk ε (d 0) hε).Exact) ∧ Mono ε ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, (CochainComplex.of T d hdd).ExactAt (p + 1)) ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, IsSplitMono (kernel.ι (d p))) ∧ (∀ p : ℕ, Injective (T p)) ∧ (r = 0 → IsZero J)
